name: Neural networks that mimic the brain
gist: These papers use spiking neural networks inspired by biology—neurons that fire only when needed—to save power and memory compared to traditional neural networks.
explain: The human brain is incredibly efficient: it uses about 20 watts of power while performing tasks that would need megawatts of electricity in a computer. Neurons are the key: they do not fire all the time. A neuron stays quiet unless it gets strong enough input to cross its threshold, at which point it spikes. This is sparse — not every neuron fires every time step. Spiking neural networks try to mimic this behavior. Instead of continuous values flowing through the network, neurons accumulate charge over time and fire only when the voltage crosses a threshold. The spike — a discrete event — then propagates.

Why is this more efficient? Because computation only happens when a neuron fires. If most neurons stay quiet, you do way less math. Additionally, spikes are discrete — you just need to send which neurons fired, not numbers — so communication between chips or parts of the brain can be compressed. The tradeoff is that spiking networks are harder to train and predict. Traditional neural networks use calculus-friendly continuous math. Spikes are discrete events that do not play well with standard learning algorithms. Researchers have developed new training methods for spiking networks, but they are still not as easy to optimize as regular networks.

These papers explore different neuron models (different threshold and charging rules), training algorithms, and applications. They measure power consumption, latency, and accuracy. Spiking networks are particularly interesting for edge devices — phones, embedded cameras, robots — where power is scarce and you want to run inference locally without draining the battery. The brain inspiration is not perfect — biological neurons are far more complex — but even a simplified spike-based model can get significant efficiency gains.

papers.title: A Spiking Heterogeneous Harmonic Resonate-and-Fire State Space Model for Time Series
papers.contribution: SH2RFSSM outperforms transformers and first-order SSMs on average across 17 datasets while eliminating matrix multiplications, suitable for resource-constrained applications.

papers.title: Resolving the Timestep Scaling Paradox in Spiking Neural Networks with a Timestep-Scalable Neuron Model
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on time-series and event-based tasks while maintaining strong performance on image classification and object detection, with improved performance when scaling timesteps.

papers.title: SmoothSpike: Spiking Transformer with Learnable Hadamard Transformation
papers.contribution: Achieves 8.2% average improvement over Spikingformer baseline on GLUE while maintaining energy efficiency.

papers.title: Towards Lossless Memory-efficient Training of Spiking Neural Networks via Gradient Checkpointing and Spike Compression
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 8× memory efficiency with ≤20% speed reduction and no accuracy loss, providing practical lossless SNN training.

papers.title: Training Deep Spiking Neural Networks without Normalization
papers.contribution: Deep SNNs train stably without normalization and outperform normalized counterparts; successfully trains 1000-layer SNN without normalization.

papers.title: 3DSMT: A Hybrid Spiking Mamba-Transformer for Point Cloud Analysis
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art among SNN-based methods on shape classification, few-shot classification, and part segmentation while significantly reducing computational energy.

papers.title: A$^2$SG: Adaptive and Asymmetric Surrogate Gradients for Training Deep Spiking Neural Networks
papers.contribution: Consistently improves accuracy and energy efficiency across CNNs and Transformers on diverse tasks including image classification and segmentation, establishing it as general reliable solution.

papers.title: Cannistraci-Hebb Training on Ultra-Sparse Spiking Neural Networks
papers.contribution: CH-SNN achieves high structural sparsity while maintaining performance comparable to fully connected networks.

papers.title: Distribution-Aware Multi-Granularity Phase Coding: Towards Lower Conversion Error for Spike-Driven Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Spiking LLM attains lowest perplexity with ANN-level accuracy accompanied by 42% reduction in latency via efficient neuromorphic hardware deployment.

papers.title: Efficient Transformer Attention for SNNs via Hadamard Simplification
papers.contribution: SSA achieves 96.38% on CIFAR-10, 79.45% on CIFAR-100, and 97.56% on DVS-Gesture while reducing computational complexity from O(N²D) to O(ND) and communication from O(N²) to O(ND).

papers.title: Efficiently Training Time-to-First-Spike Spiking Neural Networks from Scratch
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on MNIST (99.48%), Fashion-MNIST (92.90%), CIFAR10 (90.56%), CIFAR100 (70.27%), and DVS Gesture (95.83%).

papers.title: Frequency Matching in Spiking Neural Networks for mmWave Sensing
papers.contribution: 6.22% test-accuracy improvement and 3.64x energy reduction vs ANN baselines on mmWave datasets when frequency-matching LIF bandwidth to data's discriminative spectrum.

papers.title: Otters: An Energy-Efficient Spiking Transformer via Optical Time-to-First-Spike Encoding
papers.contribution: Otters achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on seven GLUE benchmark datasets with 1.77x improvement in energy efficiency over previous leading SNNs.

papers.title: Plug-and-Play Spiking Operators: Breaking the Nonlinearity Bottleneck in Spiking Transformers
papers.contribution: Supports common Transformer nonlinearities without fine-tuning with less than 1% accuracy drop across evaluated tasks.

papers.title: Positional Encoding for Spiking Transformers
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms existing SNN methods on 13 NLP benchmarks while preserving energy efficiency without additional parameters.

papers.title: Practical Mechanism for Fault-Tolerant Spiking Neural Networks via Simple Input Control Based on Learnable Fragmentation
papers.contribution: Improves fault tolerance without accessing internal circuits across various SNN models and validates effectiveness on physical FPGA platforms.

papers.title: SAFA-SNN: Sparsity-Aware On-Device Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning with Fast-Adaptive Structure of Spiking Neural Network
papers.contribution: SAFA-SNN achieves effective on-device few-shot class-incremental learning on standard and neuromorphic datasets while maintaining lower energy consumption than ANN-based approaches.

papers.title: SMixer: Rethinking Efficient-Training and Event-Driven SNNs
papers.contribution: Maintains event-driven characteristics with competitive performance while significantly reducing GPU training overhead through adaptive token and firing-rate selection.

papers.title: SVL: Empowering Spiking Neural Networks for Efficient 3D Open-World Understanding
papers.contribution: Achieves 85.4% zero-shot 3D classification and outperforms SNNs on diverse tasks (+6.1% 3D cls, +2.1% DVS actions) while enabling energy-efficient open-world understanding sometimes surpassing ANNs.

papers.title: Spik4lite: Refactoring Neuromorphic Sparsity for Efficient Spiking Neural Networks on Commodity Edge Devices
papers.contribution: Integrate Spik4lite into existing SNN baselines to improve accuracy-efficiency on real edge devices while saving computational and energy costs.

papers.title: SpikingLM: Towards Fully Spiking Language Model
papers.contribution: Reduces energy consumption by 57.9% and achieves state-of-the-art performance on GLUE with Spike2Max reducing energy by over 95% via hardware-efficient bit-shift operations.

papers.title: TEFormer: Structured Bidirectional Temporal Enhancement Modeling in Spiking Transformers
papers.contribution: Consistently and significantly outperforms SNN and Spiking Transformer baselines across benchmarks; performance gains remain stable across diverse neural encoding schemes.

papers.title: Trajectory-Aware Spiking DiTs Conversion via Membrane Potential Error-Feedback
papers.contribution: The method achieves competitive generative quality on ImageNet with superior energy efficiency for spiking diffusion transformers.

papers.title: Zeroth-Order Forward-Only SNN Training Inspiring Neuromorphic On-Chip Learning
papers.contribution: SZO achieves accuracy comparable to first-order methods with faster learning speed on model training, continual training, and unsupervised adaptation for neuromorphic on-chip learning.
